study.question: Does retaining event dispersion inside each fixed compression block, only in the existing task-specific context-history correction, improve validation click AUC over both frozen sources and the incumbent at justified measured cost? Does auxiliary adapter-context transfer interact with that change?
study.hypothesis: Observed limitation: the incumbent compresses ten events into slot means before its context-history branch applies tanh, so within-block changes that preserve the scored block sum and global detail summaries are invisible to that branch. The r0052 block-vs-aggregate gain is only 0.000069560 and later block-moment, conditioning, adjacency and mass variants did not exceed it; they operate on already-compressed blocks and do not restore the erased event distribution. Hypothesis: averaging the same tied nonlinear projection over individual, score-weighted events within a block retains complementary predictive information without extra learned capacity. Preserve the original block preactivation and center the new event departures to exact zero mean in real arithmetic; this keeps the affine mean and all existing base/detail paths fixed. Any gain is provisional until matched controls, actual costs and paired repetitions support it.
